body:
Both dangling-citation enumerations walk gw.reactor.snapshot() — the primary tier alone:
the erase receipt's manifest (src/gateway/erase.ts ~345-350) and the slate receipt's
citations (src/gateway/slate.ts ~1708-1715, documented as "the surviving deltas that dangle
at this hole"). Meanwhile the BYTE verdict in the same receipt walks primary plus every
attached pool (tierVerdicts, slate.ts ~1440-1446). So the receipt is multi-tier where it
proves absence and single-tier where it enumerates danglers.

T207 (landed 2026-08-21) makes pool-resident citations STRUCTURAL: every federated arrival
now has a receiver-signed stamp in the pool whose deltaRef pointers name it. Erase a delta
that also arrived through a channel (a peer echoing the operator's own delta): the pool copy
purges, the tiers verdict honestly reads clean, the stamp survives (receiver-authored, its
own id) — and the receipt's citations list omits it while a gather still serves a signed
delta pointing at the hole. The "POINTERS ARE NOT CONTENT" nonClaim keeps this out of
resurrection territory; the defect is the enumeration answering for tiers it never walked —
the report level of the deltasSince-under-MirrorBackend shape.

Build: widen both enumerations to walk the same tier set tierVerdicts walks (primary + each
attached pool's reactor). Shape constraint from frozen rails (T64): slate-cut.test.ts asserts
`receipt.members[0].citations` CONTAINS a bare delta id and slate-receipt.test.ts asserts it
is an array — so the id list stays string[] and tier attribution rides an ADDITIVE field
beside it, never a replacement shape.

Acceptance criteria:
(a) An erase whose target is cited by a pool-resident stamp lists that citation in the
    receipt, named to its pool. Verify: new test test/gateway/receipt-citations-tiers.test.ts.
(b) A primary-resident citation still enumerates (two-sided, no regression). Verify: same file.
(c) On the slate receipt (the one carrying `tiers` beside `citations`), the byte verdict and
    the citation enumeration name the same tier set; the erase receipt's citations carry the
    additive tier attribution. Verify: same file.

Merge tier: a report made more honest — the erasure split's self-merge side, with the
no-widening line in the PR (nothing new is purged; the receipt discloses more).
title: Erasure receipts enumerate dangling citations over the primary only — the byte verdict walks every tier
